notes.title: Polysomnography Report
notes.author: Sleep medicine physician
notes.text:
Polysomnography Report
Date: 12/04/2025
Patient: Edmond Corwin, 77-year-old male

Diagnostic in-laboratory polysomnography performed 12/04/2025. The study demonstrated significant sleep-disordered breathing. Total apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) 47.5 events/hour. Central and mixed apneas comprised 13% of all events. Sleep architecture was disrupted with frequent arousals related to respiratory events. Oxygen saturation showed intermittent desaturations corresponding to apneas and hypopneas.

In summary, the patient has severe sleep apnea with a predominance of obstructive events and a notable proportion of central and mixed apneas. These findings suggest the need for clinical evaluation and consideration of treatment options.

Sleep Medicine Consultation Note
Date: 07/11/2026
Patient: Edmond Corwin, 78-year-old male

Reason for Consultation:
Evaluation and management of sleep-disordered breathing.

History:
Mr. Corwin has a history of obstructive sleep apnea diagnosed several years ago. He reports difficulty tolerating CPAP therapy.

Physical Examination:
BMI 30.1 kg/m2.

Assessment:
Obstructive sleep apnea with documented CPAP intolerance.

Plan:
CPAP intolerance: download shows average use 2.9 hours per night on 41% of nights despite mask refitting; shared decision-making with the patient documented that CPAP is not tolerated. Alternative therapies will be considered, including possible oral appliance therapy or positional therapy. Follow-up sleep study may be scheduled to reassess severity and treatment options. Patient education provided regarding sleep hygiene and symptom monitoring.

Follow-up:
Patient to return in 3 months or sooner if symptoms worsen.
